question: how many bytes of same-origin stylesheets and scripts a first view saves when each file new to the visit is compressed against an earlier file of the same site as a dictionary, against brotli 11 alone, when the dictionary is the best earlier file (an oracle), the file a browser would pick (the most recent one in the same directory), or one base file per directory that the server chose offline
instrument: node:zlib zstd level 19 with a raw dictionary (window log 23) and node:zlib brotli quality 11; brotli command line brotli 1.2.0 with -D for brotli dictionaries; every delta decoded and compared with the file; the transfer is the compressed size, no headers

method.pages: home plus the first 4 internal pages of measurements/trim/2026-10-19.json that loaded; the files are the same-origin <link rel=stylesheet> and <script src> of each page, fetched once each in visit order with identity encoding

arms.oracle: the earlier file of the same kind with the smallest zstd delta, any directory; the brotli delta uses the same file
arms.browser: the most recent earlier file of the same kind in the same directory, as a Use-As-Dictionary match of the directory would select
arms.serverVisit: the directory base, only when the visit has already fetched it
arms.serverHeld: the directory base, as if an earlier visit had left it in the browser; chosen with every file of the crawl, the measured page included
arms.serverOut: the same, with the base chosen over the files of the other pages only, so the page measured did not pick its dictionary

method.base: per site, kind and directory with at least two files: the file with the smallest sum over the other files of min(zstd delta against it, brotli 11 alone), computed over every file of the crawl and then applied to the visit
method.fallback: a file whose delta is not smaller than brotli 11 alone is served plain, so an arm never costs bytes; the headline is the median over sites of the share of brotli 11 bytes saved over the site's new files
method.request pacing: 250 ms between requests, one request at a time

exclusions: a file the page names more than once, or on a later page, is counted at its first fetch only
a file the server answered with anything but 200
